newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bunker market unaffected by strike -traders.
newsitem.headline: Japan bunker market unaffected by strike -traders.

text.p: Japan's bunker oil prices have been little affected by a 24-hour port workers' strike that started on Wednesday, since oil barge workers belong to a different union from the ones that are striking, traders said.
"I saw no impact of the strike on (bunker) prices or on delivery schedules," a bunker trader with a trading house said.

Two port workers' unions went on strike at about 50 ports to protest against the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission's decision to impose sanctions on Japanese ships calling at U.S. ports, and also to demand better working conditions.
Workers operating oil barges, which supply bunker oil to vessels, belong to different unions from the striking ones.
Japan's bunker oil prices were assessed at around $123 per tonne for the benchmark 180 centistoke grade on Wednesday, little changed from levels late last week, traders said.
